iterations.theme: Život bl. Ivana Merza, njegova posebnost, rast štovanja i iskustva iz rada postulature

sections.subtitle: Od filipinske mladeži do zagrebačkog studija: razgovor o prvom laiku blaženiku Crkve u Hrvata
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj pozdravlja gledatelje i predstavlja gosta, p. Božidara Nagyja, u studiju podcasta
sections.content:
Epizoda podcasta **ReDefinicija** otvara se isječkom koji odmah privlači pažnju. Gost, isusovac **p. Božidar Nagy**, govori o pravoj „eksploziji“ štovanja bl. Ivana Merza. Ta se eksplozija, kako ističe, najprije dogodila daleko od Hrvatske, na Filipinima, odmah nakon beatifikacije. Merza je tamo otkrila filipinska mladež. Posebno je za to zaslužan **Dave de la Cruz**, danas doktor, koji je tada imao tek osamnaest godina.

Voditelj zatim pozdravlja gledatelje tradicionalnim „Hvaljeni Isus i Marija i sveti Josip“ i predstavlja gosta. Ne skriva da jedva čeka otvoriti današnju temu, a to je blaženi Ivan Merz. P. Nagy zahvaljuje na pozivu i upućuje srdačan pozdrav slušateljima i gledateljima. Time počinje razgovor koji vodi od Merčeva djetinjstva u Banjoj Luci do dirljivih iskustava iz višedesetljetnog rada postulature.
sections.subtitle_en: From Filipino youth to the Zagreb studio: a conversation about the first lay blessed of the Church among Croats
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host greets the viewers and introduces the guest, p. Božidar Nagy, in the podcast studio
sections.content_en:
The episode of the podcast **ReDefinicija** opens with a clip that immediately attracts attention. The guest, Jesuit **p. Božidar Nagy**, speaks about a true "explosion" of veneration of Bl. Ivan Merz. That explosion, as he points out, first occurred far from Croatia, in the Philippines, immediately after the beatification. Merz was discovered there by Filipino youth. Especially credited for this is **Dave de la Cruz**, today a doctor, who was then only eighteen years old.

The host then greets the viewers with the traditional "Praised be Jesus and Mary and Saint Joseph" and introduces the guest. He does not hide that he can hardly wait to open today's topic, which is Blessed Ivan Merz. P. Nagy thanks for the invitation and sends a warm greeting to the listeners and viewers. With this begins the conversation that leads from Merz's childhood in Banja Luka to touching experiences from decades-long work of the postulation.

sections.subtitle: Prvi vjernik laik na oltaru: titula koja Merza izdvaja
sections.screenshot_description: P. Božidar Nagy objašnjava da je Ivan Merz prvi vjernik laik blaženik u Crkvi u Hrvata
sections.content:
Na pitanje tko je bio blaženi Ivan Merz, p. Nagy kreće od njegove posljednje titule. Merz je **prvi vjernik laik u povijesti Crkve u Hrvata koji je uzdignut na oltar** kao blaženik i budući svetac.

Gost naglašava koliko je to značajno. Svi ostali hrvatski sveci i blaženici bili su svećenici, biskupi, časne sestre ili redovnici. Merz je, naprotiv, vjernik laik, i to suvremen, „moderan, iz naših dana“. Od njegove smrti uskoro će proći cijelo stoljeće, točnije za dvije godine. Ipak, kako p. Nagy kaže, „još uvijek je on tu“. Do nedavno su živjeli ljudi koji su ga osobno poznavali i s njim prijateljevali.
sections.subtitle_en: The first lay faithful on the altar: a title that sets Merz apart
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fr. Božidar Nagy explains that Ivan Merz is the first lay faithful blessed in the Church among Croats
sections.content_en:
To the question of who Blessed Ivan Merz was, Fr. Nagy starts from his last title. Merz is **the first lay faithful in the history of the Church among Croats who was raised to the altar** as a blessed and future saint.

The guest emphasizes how significant that is. All other Croatian saints and blesseds were priests, bishops, nuns, or religious. Merz is, on the contrary, a lay faithful, and a contemporary one, “modern, from our days.” A whole century will soon pass since his death, more precisely in two years. Yet, as Fr. Nagy says, “he is still here.” Until recently, people lived who knew him personally and were friends with him.

sections.subtitle: Austrougarska obitelj, željeznička stanica i čuvena banjalučka realka
sections.screenshot_description: Gost pripovijeda o Merčevu rođenju u Banjoj Luci 1896. i podrijetlu njegovih roditelja
sections.content:
Biografski se priča vraća na početak. Ivan Merz rođen je u **Banjoj Luci 1896. godine**, u obitelji koju p. Nagy opisuje kao tipično austrougarsku:

- **otac** je bio češki Nijemac iz Plzena u Češkoj,
- **majka** je bila iz Velike Kaniže u Mađarskoj.

Otac je završio vojnu akademiju i postao austrougarski časnik višeg ranga. Pretpostavljeni su ga poslali u Banju Luku, gdje je sve do preseljenja obitelji u Zagreb radio kao šef željezničke stanice.

Gost spominje i jedan mali detalj iz Merčeva školovanja. Prvi razred osnovne škole započeo je u Banjoj Luci, ali drugi i treći razred pohađao je u **Prijedoru**, jer je otac ondje bio premješten, također na željeznicu. Za četvrti razred obitelj se vratila u Banju Luku. Nakon osnovne škole Merz je upisao čuvenu **banjalučku realku**, gimnaziju u krasnoj zgradi koju je izgradila Austro-Ugarska.

Roditelji su ga dali u školu godinu dana ranije. Po Božjoj providnosti, kako primjećuje p. Nagy, to se kasnije pokazalo itekako važnim. Merz je tako **maturirao 1914. sa sedamnaest i pol godina, s odličnim uspjehom**.
sections.subtitle_en: Austro-Hungarian family, railway station, and the famous Banja Luka realka
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest recounts Merz's birth in Banja Luka in 1896 and the origins of his parents
sections.content_en:
Biographically, the story returns to the beginning. Ivan Merz was born in **Banja Luka in 1896**, in a family that Fr. Nagy describes as typically Austro-Hungarian:

- the **father** was a Czech German from Plzen in the Czech Republic,
- the **mother** was from Velika Kaniža in Hungary.

The father graduated from the military academy and became a higher-ranking Austro-Hungarian officer. Superiors sent him to Banja Luka, where he worked as the railway station master until the family's relocation to Zagreb.

The guest also mentions one small detail from Merz's schooling. He began the first grade of elementary school in Banja Luka, but he attended the second and third grade in **Prijedor**, because his father was transferred there, also to the railway. For the fourth grade, the family returned to Banja Luka. After elementary school, Merz enrolled in the famous **Banja Luka realka**, a gymnasium in a beautiful building built by Austria-Hungary.

His parents enrolled him in school a year earlier. By God's providence, as Fr. Nagy notes, this later proved to be especially important. Merz thus **graduated in 1914 at seventeen and a half years old, with excellent marks**.

sections.subtitle: „Katolik svjetovnjak spasio me za vječnost“: profesor Maraković i tajna ankete
sections.screenshot_description: P. Nagy govori o presudnom utjecaju profesora Ljubomira Marakovića na mladog Merza
sections.content:
Banjalučko razdoblje obilježio je snažan pozitivan utjecaj profesora **dr. Ljubomira Marakovića**. I on je bio izvanredan katolički laik. U Hrvatski katolički pokret uključio se još kao student književnosti u Beču, oko 1903. i 1904. godine. Na Merza je djelovao ne samo kulturno i književno nego i vjerski, pa mu je Maraković cijeli život ostao uzor.

P. Nagy zatim iznosi zanimljivu priču. Oko 1925. godine **dr. Kniewald**, kasnije Merčev veliki prijatelj, sastavljao je *Katolički đak*, molitvenik za katoličku mušku mladež. Za tu je priliku proveo veliku anonimnu anketu: intervjuirao je **400 mladića** i postavio im tridesetak pitanja. Zamolio je i Merza da ispuni upitnik. Od svih 400 odgovora jedino je Kniewald znao koji pripadaju Merzu. Odgovori su se sačuvali i danas čine svojevrsni **duhovni autoprofil** blaženika, objavljen u njegovim sabranim djelima.

Jedno je pitanje glasilo: kako su na mene, odnosno na moj vjerski život, djelovali profesori u srednjoj školi? Merz je odgovorio kratko: **„Katolik svjetovnjak spasio me za vječnost.“** Tada je imao 29 godina, tri godine prije smrti. Voditelj primjećuje da je riječ o retrogradnom pogledu. P. Nagy dodaje da su na Merza utjecale i mnoge druge osobe, ali ga je Maraković usmjerio na poseban način.

Maraković je Merza usmjerio i prema zvanju profesora književnosti. Sam se 1919. preselio u Zagreb, pokrenuo poznati časopis **Hrvatska prosvjeta** i bio vrlo cijenjen kao književni kritičar. Trebao je postati i sveučilišni profesor, ali su tada nastupili neki problemi. To je, kako gost kaže, „druga tema“.
sections.subtitle_en: „A lay Catholic saved me for eternity“: Professor Maraković and the secret of the survey
sections.screenshot_description_en: P. Nagy speaks about the decisive influence of Professor Ljubomir Maraković on the young Merz
sections.content_en:
The Banja Luka period was marked by the strong positive influence of Professor **Dr. Ljubomir Maraković**. He too was an exceptional Catholic layman. He joined the Croatian Catholic Movement back when he was a literature student in Vienna, around the years 1903 and 1904. He influenced Merz not only culturally and literarily but also religiously, so Maraković remained his role model for his entire life.

P. Nagy then relates an interesting story. Around 1925, **Dr. Kniewald**, later a great friend of Merz, was compiling *Katolički đak*, a prayer book for Catholic male youth. For that occasion, he conducted a large anonymous survey: he interviewed **400 young men** and asked them about thirty questions. He also asked Merz to fill out the questionnaire. Out of all 400 responses, only Kniewald knew which ones belonged to Merz. The responses have been preserved and today constitute a kind of **spiritual self-profile** of the blessed, published in his collected works.

One question read: how did professors in high school affect me, that is, my religious life? Merz answered briefly: **„A lay Catholic saved me for eternity.“** At that time he was 29 years old, three years before his death. The host notes that this is a retrospective view. P. Nagy adds that many other people also influenced Merz, but Maraković directed him in a special way.

Maraković also guided Merz toward the profession of literature professor. He himself moved to Zagreb in 1919, launched the well-known journal **Hrvatska prosvjeta**, and was highly esteemed as a literary critic. He was also supposed to become a university professor, but then some problems arose. That is, as the guest says, „another topic“.

sections.subtitle: Od vojne akademije do Dolomita: rat koji je razbio „estetski katolicizam“
sections.screenshot_description: Gost opisuje Merčev odlazak u vojnu akademiju i kasnije na talijansko bojište
sections.content:
Nakon mature Merz je, na želju roditelja koji su htjeli da postane časnik poput oca, upisao **vojnu akademiju u Bečkom Novom Mjestu**. Za vojništvo, međutim, nije imao nikakve volje. Nakon tri mjeseca, pred Božić 1914., napustio je akademiju. Već u siječnju upisao je fakultet u Beču.

Studij je trajao svega godinu dana jer je bjesnio **Prvi svjetski rat**. Merz je pozvan na vojnu obuku u veljači 1916., najprije u Grazu, a zatim na tečajeve na kojima je osposobljen za skijaškog vođu postrojbi u sjevernoj Italiji, u Dolomitima. Krajem 1916. poslan je na **talijansko bojište**, gdje je proveo dvije godine, sve do kraja rata.

P. Nagy ističe da je upravo ratno razdoblje na Merza najviše djelovalo u vjerskom smislu. U jednom članku Merz je sam zapisao da je do rata njegov katolicizam bio **„estetski katolicizam“**, a da je nakon rata spoznao pravi kršćanski život koji treba voditi. Život mu je bio vrlo često ugrožen, od bombi i svih drugih opasnosti, ali ga je, kako gost kaže, dragi Bog sačuvao.
sections.subtitle_en: From the military academy to the Dolomites: the war that shattered „aesthetic Catholicism“
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest describes Merz's departure to the military academy and later to the Italian front
sections.content_en:
After graduation, Merz, at the wish of his parents who wanted him to become an officer like his father, enrolled in the **military academy in Wiener Neustadt**. For military service, however, he had no desire whatsoever. After three months, before Christmas 1914, he left the academy. Already in January, he enrolled in university in Vienna.

His studies lasted only a year because **World War I** was raging. Merz was called up for military training in February 1916, first in Graz, and then to courses where he was trained as a ski leader of units in northern Italy, in the Dolomites. At the end of 1916, he was sent to the **Italian front**, where he spent two years, until the end of the war.

Fr. Nagy points out that it was precisely the wartime period that affected Merz the most in a religious sense. In one article, Merz himself wrote that before the war his Catholicism was **„aesthetic Catholicism“**, and that after the war he realized the true Christian life that ought to be led. His life was very often in danger, from bombs and all other hazards, but, as the guest says, dear God preserved him.

sections.subtitle: Beč, Pariz, Zagreb: „Umro je kao svetac jer je živio kao svetac“
sections.screenshot_description: P. Nagy govori o Merčevu studiju u Parizu i citira francuski dnevnik La Croix
sections.content:
Krajem rata 1918. Merz se u jesen vratio u Banju Luku. Već u siječnju otišao je u Beč i nastavio studij. Ondje je proveo dvije godine, 1919. i 1920. U jesen 1920. dobio je **stipendiju za Pariz** od jedne katoličke udruge. To je isposlovao isusovac **p. Miroslav Vanin**. Stipendije su dobili Merz i još dvojica dobrih katoličkih mladića. Ključnu ulogu ponovno je odigrao Maraković, koji je Merza predložio među tom trojicom.

U Parizu je Merz proveo dvije godine i skupljao materijal za doktorsku disertaciju. Nakon povratka 1922. dovršio ju je i obranio na **Zagrebačkom sveučilištu**. U Zagrebu je zatim proveo šest godina, sve do svoje svetačke smrti, i ostavio trag „kakav si čovjek može samo zamisliti jedan svetac“.

P. Nagy prenosi i ocjenu Francuza koji su ga dobro upoznali. U katoličkom dnevniku **La Croix** (Križ) napisali su: **„Ivan Merz je umro kao svetac jer je živio kao svetac.“** Voditelj to sažima riječima: „Kratko i jasno.“
sections.subtitle_en: Vienna, Paris, Zagreb: "He died as a saint because he lived as a saint"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fr. Nagy speaks about Merz's studies in Paris and quotes the French daily La Croix
sections.content_en:
At the end of the war in 1918, in the autumn, Merz returned to Banja Luka. Already in January he went to Vienna and continued his studies. He spent two years there, 1919 and 1920. In the autumn of 1920, he received a **scholarship for Paris** from a Catholic association. This was arranged by the Jesuit **Fr. Miroslav Vanin**. Scholarships were awarded to Merz and two other fine Catholic young men. A key role was once again played by Maraković, who proposed Merz among those three.

In Paris, Merz spent two years and collected material for his doctoral dissertation. After returning in 1922, he completed it and defended it at the **University of Zagreb**. He then spent six years in Zagreb, until his saintly death, leaving behind an impact "such as a man can only imagine from a saint".

Fr. Nagy also conveys the assessment of the French who got to know him well. In the Catholic daily **La Croix** (The Cross), they wrote: **"Ivan Merz died as a saint because he lived as a saint."** The host summarizes this with the words: "Short and clear."

sections.subtitle: Ratni dnevnik i program od 5. veljače 1918.: „Boga nikad ne zaboraviti“
sections.screenshot_description: Gost citira Merčeve prve životne odluke zapisane u ratnom dnevniku 5. veljače 1918.
sections.content:
Voditelj primjećuje da je Merz u kratkom vremenu proživio mnogo, što se vidi i u njegovu dnevniku i radovima. Pita gosta koje mu je razdoblje Merčeva života najzanimljivije. P. Nagy bez dvojbe izdvaja **ratni period**. U njemu je Merz vodio dnevnik u kojem se vide njegova razmišljanja o prolaznosti života i smrti. Smrti je gledao u oči gotovo svaki dan, kao i brojnim poginulima. Upravo su ti trenuci, kako gost kaže, pročišćavali njegov pogled, pa je na život počeo gledati „sasvim drugim očima“.

Potkraj rata Merz je ocu napisao: **„Zahvalan sam Bogu što sam sudjelovao u ratu jer sam u ratu spoznao tolike stvari koje inače nikad ne bih spoznao.“** Dodao je da jedva čeka vratiti se kući i uskladiti život s pravim kršćanskim smislom, „i tako je i bilo“.

P. Nagy posebno ističe jedan datum koji gledatelji mogu sami provjeriti u ratnom dnevniku: **5. veljače 1918.** Toga je dana Merz zapisao svoj prvi životni program, odnosno odluke kako će živjeti nakon rata. Program počinje rečenicom: **„Boga nikad, nikad ne zaboraviti. Uvijek težiti za sjedinjenjem s Njime.“** Slijede odluke o postu, asketskom životu i molitvi. Gost taj tekst preporučuje svima.

Merz je svoje odluke cijeli život usavršavao i nadopunjavao. Svake je godine obavljao duhovne vježbe i na njima donosio nove odluke. One sa zadnjih duhovnih vježbi napisao je na pisaćem stroju i stavio u **misal** iz kojega je svakodnevno pratio misu. S tim je misalom otišao i na operaciju u bolnicu, tako da su ga odluke pratile praktički do smrti. Voditelj zaključuje da ga je rat formirao i da se ta formacija dalje prenosi.
sections.subtitle_en: War diary and program of February 5, 1918: "Never forget God"
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest quotes Merz's first life resolutions recorded in his war diary on February 5, 1918.
sections.content_en:
The host notes that Merz lived through a great deal in a short time, which is evident both in his diary and his works. He asks the guest which period of Merz's life is most interesting to him. Fr. Nagy singles out without hesitation the **war period**. During it, Merz kept a diary showing his reflections on the transience of life and death. He looked death in the eyes almost every day, as well as numerous deceased. It was precisely those moments, as the guest says, that purified his vision, so he began to look at life "with completely different eyes."

Toward the end of the war, Merz wrote to his father: **"I am grateful to God that I took part in the war because during the war I came to realize so many things that I otherwise never would have realized."** He added that he could hardly wait to return home and align his life with the true Christian meaning, "and that is how it was."

Fr. Nagy highlights in particular one date that viewers can check for themselves in the war diary: **February 5, 1918.** On that day, Merz wrote down his first life program, that is, resolutions on how he would live after the war. The program begins with the sentence: **"Never, never forget God. Always strive for union with Him."** Resolutions on fasting, ascetic life, and prayer follow. The guest recommends this text to everyone.

Merz perfected and supplemented his resolutions throughout his entire life. Every year he made spiritual exercises and made new resolutions during them. Those from his last spiritual exercises he typed on a typewriter and placed into the **missal** from which he followed Mass daily. With that missal he also went to the hospital for surgery, so that the resolutions accompanied him practically until death. The host concludes that the war formed him and that this formation continues to be passed on.

sections.subtitle: Svetost za katedrom: profesor francuskog i njemačkog kao uzor laicima
sections.screenshot_description: P. Nagy objašnjava kako je Merz ostvario svetost u svjetovnom zanimanju
sections.content:
Voditelj zatim postavlja pitanje koje često čuje: nisu li svi sveci isti? Po čemu je onda Ivan Merz specifičan?

P. Nagy odgovara da je Merz prije svega **prvi laik u Crkvi u Hrvata kojemu je službeno priznata svetost života**. Ima, dodaje, još mnogo vjernika laika koje bi bilo vrijedno uzdići na oltar, ali to je dug proces. Kod Merza je prepoznato da je kreposti živio u herojskom stupnju.

Merz je pokazao da je moguće **živjeti kao svjetovnjak u svijetu, imati svjetovno zanimanje i postati svetac**. Nakon studija književnosti bio je profesor **francuskog i njemačkog jezika na Nadbiskupskoj gimnaziji**. Gost naglašava da je bez obzira na to što je škola bila nadbiskupijska predavao običan, svjetovni predmet. Nije predavao vjeronauk. Upravo je vršeći to svakodnevno zanimanje ostvarivao svetost života.
sections.subtitle_en: Holiness at the lectern: professor of French and German as a model for the laity
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fr. Nagy explains how Merz achieved holiness in a secular occupation
sections.content_en:
The host then asks a question he often hears: are not all saints the same? What makes Ivan Merz specific then?

Fr. Nagy answers that Merz is above all **the first layperson in the Church among Croats whose holiness of life was officially recognized**. There are, he adds, still many lay faithful who would be worthy of being raised to the altar, but that is a long process. In Merz's case, it was recognized that he lived the virtues to a heroic degree.

Merz showed that it is possible **to live as a layperson in the world, have a secular occupation, and become a saint**. After studying literature, he was a professor of **French and German at the Nadbiskupska gimnazija**. The guest emphasizes that regardless of the fact that the school was archdiocesan, he taught an ordinary, secular subject. He did not teach religious education. It was precisely by carrying out that daily occupation that he achieved holiness of life.

sections.subtitle: Pet poruka jedne slike: kravata, knjiga, tornjevi, golub i euharistija
sections.screenshot_description: P. Nagy pokazuje sliku bl. Ivana Merza autora Ante Mamuše koja visi iza sugovornika
sections.content:
P. Nagy upozorava gledatelje na sliku iza sugovornika. Naslikao ju je **Anto Mamuša**, akademski slikar iz Novog Travnika u Bosni, poznat po brojnim religioznim motivima. Prema gostovim riječima, slikar je na njoj savršeno prikazao profil blaženika. Iz slike se može iščitati **pet poruka**:

- **Laik u civilu.** Mladi čovjek s kravatom pod vratom živio je u svijetu, imao svjetovno zanimanje i ostvario svetost.
- **Knjiga.** Simbol učenosti, kulture i znanosti. Merz je povezao vjeru, znanost i kulturu i pokazao da one ne samo mogu nego i *trebaju* ići zajedno. Doktorat pod naslovom *Utjecaj liturgije na francuske književnike* objavljen je u Parizu nakon beatifikacije. Francuzi su ocijenili da je Merz obradio temu koju dotad nitko od njih nije obradio, pa ga književni krugovi ondje vrlo cijene. Njegov duhovnik **p. Vrbanek** svjedočio je da je Merz poznavao deset jezika: pet je lijepo govorio, a na pet je imao pasivno znanje. Voditelj ga naziva „pravim eruditom“.
- **Tornjevi crkava.** Na slici su banjalučka katedrala, zagrebačka katedrala i Bazilika sv. Petra. Oni izražavaju Merčevu duboku crkvenost. Njegov prijatelj **Dušan Žanko** rekao je da u liku Ivana Merza nema jače ideje od ideje Crkve, koja kroz liturgiju daje hvalu Bogu, a preko hijerarhije i papinstva čuva jedinstvo.
- **Bijeli golub, simbol Duha Svetoga.** Duh Sveti nadahnjivao je i vodio Merza te od njega učinio velikog apostola i svjedoka vjere, kao što je nekoć promijenio apostole.
- **Euharistija.** Prikazana je pokraj njegove glave jer je bila sastavni dio njegove duhovnosti. Već kao student svakodnevno je išao na misu i pričest, osobito u Zagrebu. To je nedavno u propovijedi na blagdan blaženika u Zagrebu posebno istaknuo i banjalučki biskup **Franjo Komarica**.

To su, zaključuje p. Nagy, poruke kojima Merz svjedoči i koje vjernici mogu nasljedovati.
sections.subtitle_en: Five Messages of One Painting: Tie, Book, Towers, Dove, and Eucharist
sections.screenshot_description_en: P. Nagy points to the painting of Bl. Ivan Merz by Anto Mamuša hanging behind the interlocutor
sections.content_en:
P. Nagy draws the viewers' attention to the painting behind the interlocutor. It was painted by **Anto Mamuša**, an academic painter from Novi Travnik in Bosnia, known for numerous religious motifs. According to the guest's words, the painter perfectly depicted the profile of the blessed on it. **Five messages** can be read from the painting:

- **A layman in civilian clothes.** A young man with a tie around his neck lived in the world, had a secular profession, and attained holiness.
- **A book.** A symbol of erudition, culture, and science. Merz connected faith, science, and culture and showed that they not only can but *should* go together. His doctoral dissertation entitled *The Influence of the Liturgy on French Writers* was published in Paris after the beatification. The French assessed that Merz dealt with a topic that none of them had dealt with until then, so literary circles there hold him in high esteem. His spiritual director **p. Vrbanek** testified that Merz knew ten languages: he spoke five well, and had passive knowledge of five. The host calls him a „true erudite”.
- **Church towers.** In the painting are the Banja Luka Cathedral, the Zagreb Cathedral, and St. Peter's Basilica. They express Merz's deep ecclesiality. His friend **Dušan Žanko** said that in the figure of Ivan Merz there is no stronger idea than the idea of the Church, which through the liturgy gives praise to God, and through the hierarchy and the papacy preserves unity.
- **A white dove, symbol of the Holy Spirit.** The Holy Spirit inspired and guided Merz and made him a great apostle and witness of faith, just as He once transformed the apostles.
- **The Eucharist.** It is depicted next to his head because it was an integral part of his spirituality. Already as a student, he went to Mass and Holy Communion every day, especially in Zagreb. This was also specially emphasized recently in a homily on the feast day of the blessed in Zagreb by the Bishop of Banja Luka, **Franjo Komarica**.

These are, concludes p. Nagy, the messages to which Merz bears witness and which believers can imitate.

sections.subtitle: Zaboravljeni blaženik u novom zamahu
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj uspoređuje porast štovanja bl. Ivana Merza s 'eksplozijom' štovanja sv. Josipa
sections.content:
Voditelj iznosi svoj dojam. Iako je Merz 2003. u Banjoj Luci uzdignut na oltar, njegovo je štovanje posljednjih desetljeća bilo prilično zanemareno. Tek sada, smatra, dolazi do prave „eksplozije“ štovanja i nove valorizacije njegova lika i djela.

Kao primjer navodi da u Zagrebu postoje praktički dvije zajednice koje Merza štuju i formiraju se na njegovu primjeru. Među njima je i bratstvo **Vitezovi Bezgrešnog Srca Marijina**, koje prolazi formaciju po blaženom Ivanu Merzu. Voditelj napominje da sam Merz to nije tako nazivao jer je riječ o današnjem terminu. Povlači i usporedbu sa **sv. Josipom**, koji je stoljećima bio skriven, a danas doživljava pravi procvat štovanja. Pita gosta što je uzrok tome.

P. Nagy odgovara: „Konačno, Bogu hvala da je došlo do toga.“ Dodaje, međutim, da se prva eksplozija dogodila dvadeset godina ranije, na Filipinima, odmah nakon beatifikacije.
sections.subtitle_en: A Forgotten Blessed in a New Momentum
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host compares the rise of devotion to Bl. Ivan Merz with the 'explosion' of devotion to St. Joseph
sections.content_en:
The host shares his impression. Although Merz was raised to the altar in Banja Luka in 2003, devotion to him has been rather neglected in recent decades. Only now, he believes, is there a true "explosion" of devotion and a new appreciation of his life and work.

As an example, he mentions that in Zagreb there are practically two communities that venerate Merz and are formed according to his example. Among them is the brotherhood **Vitezovi Bezgrešnog Srca Marijina**, which undergoes formation according to Blessed Ivan Merz. The host notes that Merz himself did not call it that because it is a contemporary term. He also draws a comparison with **Saint Joseph**, who was hidden for centuries and today is experiencing a true flourishing of devotion. He asks the guest what the cause of this is.

Fr. Nagy replies: "Finally, thank God that it has come to this." He adds, however, that the first explosion occurred twenty years earlier, in the Philippines, immediately after the beatification.

sections.subtitle: Domaća zadaća koja je promijenila život: kako je Dave de la Cruz „proguglao“ Merza
sections.screenshot_description: P. Nagy prepričava kako je mladi Filipinac na internetu otkrio bl. Ivana Merza
sections.content:
P. Nagy naglašava da nitko iz Hrvatske nije išao širiti Merčevo štovanje na Filipine. Priču mu je ispričao sam **Dave de la Cruz**, tada osamnaestogodišnjak. Bio je dobar ministrant, usko povezan s Crkvom, pa ga je župnik poslao na liturgijski tečaj u njegovu gradu.

Profesor je polaznicima zadao domaću zadaću: pronaći na internetu svece posebno povezane s liturgijom. Poslušni student u tražilicu je upisao „sveci liturgija“. Kako je kasnije ispričao, **prvo ime koje se pojavilo na ekranu bilo je Ivan Merz**. Za njega nikad nije čuo.

Postulatura je tada već imala web stranicu i dosta tekstova prevedenih na engleski. Mladić je sve pročitao i oduševio se, „nešto ga je zapalilo“. Odmah se javio postulaturi i tražio što više podataka. Poslali su mu slike, sličice i relikvije druge klase. Uz pomoć roditelja, koji su bili boljeg imovinskog stanja, **2007. doputovao je avionom u Zagreb na Merčev grob**.

U Zagrebu je dobio dodatne informacije i literaturu. Po povratku je osnovao **udrugu mladih** koja štuje svece, a na poseban način bl. Ivana Merza. Udruga danas broji oko **200 članova** i ima vlastiti centar, kuću. P. Nagy primjećuje da takvo nešto „mi još nemamo ovdje“. U kući je kapelica bl. Ivana Merza s relikvijama i slikama, „upravo nešto nevjerojatno“. Sve se to može vidjeti na njihovoj web stranici.
sections.subtitle_en: Homework that changed a life: how Dave de la Cruz "Googled" Merz
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fr. Nagy recounts how a young Filipino discovered Bl. Ivan Merz on the internet
sections.content_en:
Fr. Nagy emphasizes that no one from Croatia went to spread devotion to Merz in the Philippines. The story was told to him by **Dave de la Cruz** himself, who was eighteen years old at the time. He was a good altar server, closely connected to the Church, so his parish priest sent him to a liturgical course in his city.

The professor gave the participants a homework assignment: to find on the internet saints particularly connected to the liturgy. The obedient student typed "saints liturgy" into the search engine. As he later recounted, **the first name that appeared on the screen was Ivan Merz**. He had never heard of him.

At that time, the postulation already had a website and quite a few texts translated into English. The young man read everything and was thrilled, "something ignited him". He immediately contacted the postulation and asked for as much information as possible. They sent him pictures, holy cards, and second-class relics. With the help of his parents, who were of better financial standing, **in 2007 he traveled by plane to Zagreb to Merz's tomb**.

In Zagreb, he received additional information and literature. Upon his return, he founded a **youth association** that venerates saints, and in a special way Bl. Ivan Merz. Today, the association has about **200 members** and has its own center, a house. Fr. Nagy notes that "we do not have something like that here yet". In the house is a chapel of Bl. Ivan Merz with relics and pictures, "truly something incredible". All of this can be seen on their website.

sections.subtitle: Vicepostulatura na Filipinima i 7000 potpisa za kanonizaciju
sections.screenshot_description: Gost govori o imenovanju Davea de la Cruza vicepostulatorom i prikupljanju potpisa za papu
sections.content:
Kad su u postulaturi vidjeli kako se štovanje širi, **Dave de la Cruz imenovan je vicepostulatorom**. U međuvremenu je završio studij teologije i filozofije, ali je ostao laik i pridružio se dominikanskom redu kao trećoredac. Prema crkvenim propisima, kako objašnjava p. Nagy, ondje gdje se štovanje širi izvan matične zemlje mora postojati vicepostulatura. Tako je ona osnovana i na Filipinima.

Filipinska mladež prošle je godine, kako gost kaže, „napravila čudo“ koje u Hrvatskoj nikome nije palo na pamet. Prikupili su **7000 potpisa** na molbu Svetom Ocu, novom papi, za proglašenje blaženika svetim. Molba je svečano predana Kongregaciji, a prefekt ju je predao papi, koji ju je primio i zahvalio. Voditelj dodaje da se sada čekaju odgovor i reakcija.
sections.subtitle_en: Vice-postulation in the Philippines and 7,000 Signatures for Canonization
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about the appointment of Dave de la Cruz as vice-postulator and the collection of signatures for the pope
sections.content_en:
When they saw in the postulation how the devotion was spreading, **Dave de la Cruz was appointed vice-postulator**. In the meantime, he completed studies in theology and philosophy, but remained a layman and joined the Dominican Order as a tertiary. According to Church regulations, as Fr. Nagy explains, wherever devotion spreads outside the home country, a vice-postulation must exist. Thus, one was established in the Philippines as well.

Last year, the Filipino youth, as the guest says, „performed a miracle“ that occurred to no one in Croatia. They collected **7,000 signatures** on a petition to the Holy Father, the new pope, for declaring the blessed a saint. The petition was solemnly delivered to the Congregation, and the prefect delivered it to the pope, who received it and gave thanks. The host adds that a response and reaction are now awaited.

sections.subtitle: Vrhunac rada postulature i susret koji je premostio šest desetljeća
sections.screenshot_description: P. Nagy pripovijeda o otkriću sestre benediktinke na čijem je oblačenju 1921. bio Merz
sections.content:
Voditelj podsjeća da p. Nagy nije prvi, nego drugi postulator Merčeve kauze, te ga pita koji mu je trenutak bio najzanimljiviji. Gost kaže da je vrhunac svega bila **beatifikacija**, koju je dočekao nakon mnogo truda i rada. Kao osobno najdirljivije iskustvo ipak izdvaja jedno otkriće.

Kao student u Parizu Merz je **4. studenoga 1921.** prisustvovao oblačenju mlade djevojke koja je ulazila u benediktinski samostan. Bila je jedinica u obitelji i kći generala francuske vojske iz Prvog svjetskog rata. Sa 19 godina sve je ostavila i posvetila se Bogu. Duboko dirnut, Merz je iste večeri u dnevnik zapisao dojmove: **„Danas sam sudjelovao na oblačenju jedne sestre novakinje benediktinke. Liturgija veličajna. Djevojka ostavlja svijet, ulazi da se potpuno posveti Bogu.“** P. Nagy taj prekrasni opis preporučuje svima.

Ime djevojke Merz nije zapisao. Ostavio je samo tri podatka: samostan sestara benediktinki u ulici **Rue Monsieur**, datum i to da je djevojka kći francuskog generala.

P. Nagy postao je postulator **1972.** Godine 1979. s petoricom kolega boravio je tri mjeseca u Parizu na takozvanoj trećoj probaciji, završnoj formaciji isusovačkog reda. Prvog slobodnog dana otišao je u spomenutu ulicu, ali samostana više nije bilo. Rekli su mu da je prestao postojati 1939. Sestre su se, zbog neriješenih vlasničkih odnosa, preselile u novi samostan nekih 15 km od Pariza (u transkriptu zabilježen kao Boileau-Nocaze) i dali mu broj telefona.

Nakon ručka nazvao je samostan. Sestri vratarici predstavio se kao isusovac iz Hrvatske i iznio tri podatka. Voditelj napominje da je otada prošlo gotovo 60 godina, a između je bio i Drugi svjetski rat. Vratarica je otišla pitati sestre okupljene na rekreaciji poslije ručka. Nakon tri minute vratila se riječima: **„Pater, imate nevjerojatnu sreću.“** Sestra je bila živa i među njima. Zvala se **Marie-Denise Chaville** i jedina je toga dana ušla u samostan, a otac joj je bio general.

P. Nagyju su, kako priznaje, od ganuća gotovo došle suze. Imao je dojam da se preselio pedeset godina unatrag. Poručio je sestri da će za nekoliko dana doći isusovac iz Hrvatske i donijeti joj opis njezina oblačenja kako ga je doživio jedan mladi hrvatski student. Tekst je dao prevesti i posjetio je. Bio je to, kaže, izvanredno dirljiv susret. Sestra dotad nikad nije čula za Merza, a cijeli ga je samostan potom prihvatio. Njezin je život tekao upravo onako kako je Merz gotovo proročki predvidio. Umrla je oko **1989.** u dubokoj starosti, s 90 godina. P. Nagy bio je na njezinu sprovodu jer je tada ponovno služio u Parizu.
sections.subtitle_en: The culmination of the work of the postulation and an encounter that bridged six decades
sections.screenshot_description_en: P. Nagy recounts the discovery of the Benedictine sister at whose clothing ceremony Merz was present in 1921
sections.content_en:
The host reminds that P. Nagy is not the first, but the second postulator of Merz's cause, and asks him which moment was the most interesting to him. The guest says that the culmination of everything was the **beatification**, which he lived to see after much effort and work. As his personally most touching experience, however, he singles out one discovery.

As a student in Paris, on **November 4, 1921**, Merz attended the clothing ceremony of a young girl entering a Benedictine monastery. She was an only child in the family and the daughter of a French army general from World War I. At 19 years of age, she left everything and consecrated herself to God. Deeply moved, that same evening Merz wrote his impressions in his diary: **"Today I took part in the clothing ceremony of a Benedictine novice sister. Liturgy magnificent. The girl leaves the world, enters to consecrate herself completely to God."** P. Nagy recommends this beautiful description to everyone.

Merz did not write down the girl's name. He left only three pieces of information: the monastery of the Benedictine sisters on the street **Rue Monsieur**, the date, and that the girl was the daughter of a French general.

P. Nagy became postulator in **1972**. In the year 1979, with five colleagues, he stayed for three months in Paris on the so-called third probation, the final formation of the Jesuit order. On his first free day he went to the mentioned street, but the monastery was no longer there. They told him that it had ceased to exist in 1939. Due to unresolved property relations, the sisters had moved to a new monastery some 15 km from Paris (recorded in the transcript as Boileau-Nocaze), and they gave him the telephone number.

After lunch he called the monastery. To the sister portress he introduced himself as a Jesuit from Croatia and presented the three pieces of information. The host notes that almost 60 years had passed since then, and World War II had taken place in between. The portress went to ask the sisters gathered for recreation after lunch. After three minutes she returned with the words: **"Father, you have incredible luck."** The sister was alive and among them. Her name was **Marie-Denise Chaville** and she was the only one who entered the monastery that day, and her father was a general.

P. Nagy, as he admits, almost had tears come to his eyes from emotion. He had the impression that he had moved fifty years back in time. He sent word to the sister that in a few days a Jesuit from Croatia would come and bring her the description of her clothing ceremony as experienced by a young Croatian student. He had the text translated and visited her. It was, he says, an extraordinarily touching encounter. Until then, the sister had never heard of Merz, and the entire monastery subsequently embraced him. Her life unfolded exactly as Merz had almost prophetically predicted. She died around **1989** in advanced old age, at 90 years of age. P. Nagy was at her funeral because he was serving in Paris again at that time.

sections.subtitle: Živa svjedočanstva i srećka koja je platila grob na Mirogoju
sections.screenshot_description: Gost pripovijeda o lutrijskoj srećki pronađenoj u Merčevu novčaniku
sections.content:
P. Nagy dodaje da je tijekom rada na beatifikaciji susreo mnoge ljude koji su Merza osobno poznavali i dali o njemu prekrasna svjedočanstva. Sva su snimljena, zapisana i sačuvana. Voditelj to opisuje kao velik posao i istodobno „vremeplov u prošlost“.

Gost zatim govori o uslišanjima. Zabilježeno ih je **oko 600 raznih vrsta**. Posebno ističe ona za koja se nitko nije molio, nego je blaženik, kako kaže, sam intervenirao, i to za vlastiti grob.

Merz je najprije pokopan na **Mirogoju**. Nekoliko dana nakon sinove smrti otac je raspremao njegove stvari i u novčaniku, koji se i danas čuva u Merčevu muzeju, pronašao **lutrijsku srećku**. Izvlačenje je bilo zakazano za kraj svibnja 1928. Otac ju je za svaki slučaj sačuvao. Srećka je dobila **750 tadašnjih jugoslavenskih dinara**, točno onoliko koliko je otac platio grobno mjesto na Mirogoju. Voditelj kaže da mu je ta zgoda već bila poznata.
sections.subtitle_en: Living testimonies and the lottery ticket that paid for the grave at Mirogoj
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest tells about the lottery ticket found in Merz's wallet
sections.content_en:
Fr. Nagy adds that during the work on the beatification he met many people who knew Merz personally and gave wonderful testimonies about him. All of them were recorded, written down, and preserved. The host describes this as a big job and at the same time a "time machine into the past".

The guest then speaks about answered prayers. **Around 600 of various kinds** have been recorded. He particularly highlights those for which no one prayed, but the blessed, as he says, intervened himself, and that for his own grave.

Merz was first buried at **Mirogoj**. A few days after his son's death, the father was clearing out his things and in the wallet, which is still kept today in the Merz Museum, found a **lottery ticket**. The drawing was scheduled for the end of May 1928. The father kept it just in case. The ticket won **750 Yugoslav dinars of that time**, exactly as much as the father paid for the grave plot at Mirogoj. The host says that that story was already known to him.

sections.subtitle: Prazna blagajna i neočekivani donator: kako je blaženik „sam platio“ novi grob
sections.screenshot_description: P. Nagy opisuje trenutak kada je nepoznati gospodin položio novac za grob na stol
sections.content:
Druga slična zgoda dogodila se pri prijenosu Merčevih posmrtnih ostataka s Mirogoja u **Baziliku Srca Isusova u Zagrebu** u prosincu 1977. Grob je iskopan na desnoj strani bazilike, kod oltara sv. Alojzija. Zidarski radovi bili su zahtjevni i stajali su blizu **900.000 tadašnjih dinara**, točnije 880.000 prema računu.

Nakon nekoliko dana, u petak, zidar je došao po isplatu, a blagajna postulature bila je potpuno prazna. P. Nagy, tada vjeroučitelj u Palmotićevoj, upravo se spremao s mladima na susret s mladim Slovencima. Zamolio je zidara da dođe u ponedjeljak. U sebi je već računao da će morati otići poglavaru i posuditi novac.

U ponedjeljak se zidar nije pojavio. Poslijepodne je iz župnog ureda nazvao kolega **p. Lozuk**: došao je neki gospodin u vezi s grobom i nekim novcem. P. Nagy je pomislio da je riječ o zidaru i predložio da dođe sutradan. Kolega ga je ispravio: gospodin nije došao po novac, nego ga *dati*. „Pa ako je za dat, nek dođe“, odgovorio je.

Došao je gospodin nižeg rasta, kako ga gost opisuje, „vrlo produhovljen“. Rekao je da je osobno poznavao Merza i bio u **orlovskoj organizaciji**, te da želi financijski pridonijeti uređenju groba. P. Nagy mu je iskreno priznao da ni dotadašnji radovi još nisu plaćeni. Gospodin je pogledao račun, pregledao stavke, rekao „U redu“, otvorio novčanik i na stol položio **900.000 dinara**.

„Ostao sam bez teksta“, prisjeća se p. Nagy. Na pitanje zašto je došao baš tada, donator je odgovorio da je dobio poticaj da mora nešto učiniti za blaženog Merza. Sutradan prijepodne zidar je bio isplaćen, ne sluteći ništa o tome što se dogodilo. Voditelj zaključuje: **„Blaženi Merz se opet pobrinuo za svoje.“** P. Nagy dodaje, uz smijeh, da se raspričao i da ga je voditelj trebao prekinuti.
sections.subtitle_en: An empty cashbox and an unexpected donor: how the blessed "paid for" his new grave himself
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fr. Nagy describes the moment when an unknown gentleman placed the money for the grave on the table
sections.content_en:
Another similar incident occurred during the transfer of Merz's mortal remains from Mirogoj to the **Bazilika Srca Isusova u Zagrebu** in December 1977. The grave was dug on the right side of the basilica, near the altar of St. Aloysius. The masonry work was demanding and cost nearly **900,000 dinars of that time**, specifically 880,000 according to the bill.

After a few days, on Friday, the mason came for payment, and the postulation's cashbox was completely empty. Fr. Nagy, then a catechist in Palmotićeva, was just preparing to go with the youth to a meeting with young Slovenians. He asked the mason to come on Monday. Inwardly, he was already calculating that he would have to go to the superior and borrow money.

On Monday, the mason did not show up. In the afternoon, a colleague, **p. Lozuk**, called from the parish office: a gentleman had arrived regarding the grave and some money. Fr. Nagy thought it was about the mason and suggested he come the next day. His colleague corrected him: the gentleman had not come for money, but to *give* it. "Well, if it is to give, let him come," he replied.

A shorter gentleman arrived, whom the guest describes as "very spiritualized." He said that he personally knew Merz and had been in the **orlovska organizacija**, and that he wanted to contribute financially to the arrangement of the grave. Fr. Nagy honestly admitted to him that the work done so far had not yet been paid for either. The gentleman looked at the bill, reviewed the items, said "All right," opened his wallet, and placed **900,000 dinars** on the table.

"I was speechless," recalls Fr. Nagy. When asked why he had come precisely then, the donor replied that he felt an impulse that he had to do something for Blessed Merz. The next morning the mason was paid, suspecting nothing of what had happened. The host concludes: **"Blessed Merz took care of his own again."** Fr. Nagy adds, laughing, that he had talked too much and that the host should have interrupted him.

sections.subtitle: Vjera koja se ne skriva: Merz i javno svjedočenje
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj pita p. Božidara Nagyja kako bi blaženi Ivan Merz gledao na javnu molitvu krunice
sections.content:
Nakon niza anegdota iz rada postulature, p. Božidar Nagy u šali primjećuje da se previše raspričao i da ga je voditelj trebao prekinuti. Voditelj odgovara da mu je bilo žao to učiniti. Zatim prelazi na pitanje koje je zajednici okupljenoj oko podcasta posebno blisko: **kako je Ivan Merz gledao na javno svjedočenje vjere** i što bi mislio o javnoj molitvi krunice.

Odgovor je jednoznačan. Merz je, ističe p. Nagy, *i te kako* bio za javno svjedočenje vjere. Kao dokaz navodi jedno njegovo „čuveno pismo”, objavljeno u Merzovim Sabranim djelima. Odmah zatim uzima sedmi svezak koji je voditelj imao pri ruci (on kaže da su „svi tu”) i počinje tražiti ulomak. Pritom napominje da se to isplati jer je riječ o „tako zanimljivom tekstu”.

Traženje traje nekoliko trenutaka. Prvo nailazi na pismo koje je Merz iz Pariza uputio roditeljima, a zatim pronalazi pravo: pismo profesoru **Ljubomiru Marakoviću**, s kojim je Merz vodio intenzivnu prepisku.
sections.subtitle_en: Faith that is not hidden: Merz and public witnessing
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host asks Fr. Božidar Nagy how Blessed Ivan Merz would view the public prayer of the Rosary
sections.content_en:
After a series of anecdotes from the work of the postulation, Fr. Božidar Nagy jokingly remarks that he has talked too much and that the host should have interrupted him. The host replies that he was sorry to do so. Then he moves to a question that is especially close to the community gathered around the podcast: **how Ivan Merz viewed the public witnessing of faith** and what he would think about the public prayer of the Rosary.

The answer is unequivocal. Merz was, Fr. Nagy points out, *very much* in favor of the public witnessing of faith. As proof, he cites one of his "famous letters," published in Merz's Collected Works. Immediately afterward, he takes the seventh volume that the host had at hand (he says that "they are all here") and begins looking for the excerpt. At the same time, he notes that it is worth it because it is "such an interesting text."

The search lasts a few moments. First, he comes across a letter that Merz sent to his parents from Paris, and then he finds the right one: a letter to Professor **Ljubomir Maraković**, with whom Merz had an intensive correspondence.

sections.subtitle: „Na nama je krivnja”: oštro pismo iz Pariza
sections.screenshot_description: P. Božidar Nagy čita naglas Merzovo pismo Marakoviću iz sedmog sveska Sabranih djela
sections.content:
Prema uvodnoj bilješci koju p. Nagy čita, Merz u tom pismu svome profesoru Marakoviću iznosi **apostolski program** koji želi ostvarivati u domovini nakon povratka sa studija u Parizu. Najvažniji dio nalazi se na kraju pisma, a p. Nagy ga čita u cijelosti:

> „Iako katolicizam u Europi sada raste, ipak je u užasnoj regresiji. I spoznavši, osjetivši u Lurdu upravo na silan način da je cijelo čovječanstvo ta mrvica stvorena da odaje poštovanje neizmjernom Bogu, a kad tamo države, zakoni, radnici, zidari, cijeli činovnički aparat funkcionira kao mašina, kao da Bog ne postoji. Čovjeku se zgrozi kad to pomisli. A tko je kriv? Dobri, jer nisu bolji.”

Merz zatim nastavlja i krivnju ne pripisuje svijetu, nego samim vjernicima:

> „Čovječanstvo jednostavno ne zna da Bog postoji, jer katolici, mjesto da se mole na javnim mjestima, mjesto da napuste svaki položaj ako je u protuslovlju s vjerom, oni se sakriju kad se Bogu mole, pričešćuju kad nije nitko u crkvi. Na nama je krivnja.”

Pismo završava usporedbom s prvim kršćanima. Oni su u odnosu na rimsku religiju bili „tako zvani veleizdajnici”, u opoziciji prema poganskoj državi i okolini, te su bili bičevani i bacani u tamnice. Današnji kršćani, piše Merz, „zašute čim vide opasnost”.

Voditelj nakon čitanja kratko zaključuje da je time sve rečeno. P. Nagy se slaže: stav je izrečen posve jasno. Dodaje da bi se Merz, kad bi danas živio i čuo za molitelje krunice na javnim mjestima, „među prvima” pridružio. Voditelj nadovezuje da bi takvu inicijativu možda i sam pokrenuo, što p. Nagy potvrđuje.
sections.subtitle_en: „The guilt is on us”: a sharp letter from Paris
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fr. Božidar Nagy reads aloud Merz's letter to Maraković from the seventh volume of the Collected Works
sections.content_en:
According to the introductory note that Fr. Nagy reads, Merz in that letter presents to his professor Maraković an **apostolic program** that he wants to realize in his homeland after returning from his studies in Paris. The most important part is found at the end of the letter, and Fr. Nagy reads it in its entirety:

> „Although Catholicism in Europe is now growing, it is nevertheless in terrible regression. And having recognized, having felt in Lourdes in a truly powerful way that all of humanity is that crumb created to give reverence to the immense God, yet out there states, laws, workers, masons, the entire bureaucratic apparatus functions like a machine, as if God does not exist. One is horrified when one thinks of this. And who is to blame? The good, because they are not better.”

Merz then continues and does not attribute the blame to the world, but to the believers themselves:

> „Humanity simply does not know that God exists, because Catholics, instead of praying in public places, instead of leaving every position if it is in contradiction with the faith, they hide when they pray to God, receive Communion when no one is in church. The guilt is on us.”

The letter ends with a comparison to the first Christians. In relation to the Roman religion, they were „so-called traitors”, in opposition to the pagan state and surroundings, and they were scourged and thrown into dungeons. Today's Christians, Merz writes, „fall silent as soon as they see danger”.

After the reading, the host briefly concludes that with this, everything has been said. Fr. Nagy agrees: the stance has been expressed completely clearly. He adds that Merz, if he were alive today and heard about those who pray the Rosary in public places, would join „among the first”. The host adds that he might have launched such an initiative himself, which Fr. Nagy confirms.

sections.subtitle: Dvaput dnevno s krunicom preko Trga bana Jelačića
sections.screenshot_description: P. Božidar Nagy opisuje Merzov svakodnevni put preko Trga bana Jelačića s krunicom u džepu
sections.content:
Merz o javnoj molitvi nije samo pisao, nego ju je i živio. P. Nagy otkriva detalj iz njegove zagrebačke svakodnevice. Merz je stanovao blizu kolodvora, u **Starčevićevu domu**, a radio je na **Kaptolu**, u gimnaziji. Zato je **svaki dan dvaput prelazio Trg bana Jelačića s krunicom u džepu** i molio je na putu na posao i s posla.

Voditelj u tome prepoznaje izravnu poveznicu s današnjom praksom javne molitve na glavnom zagrebačkom trgu. Merz je, kaže voditelj, svojom molitvom krunice praktički posvećivao Trg. Upravo to danas čine molitelji koji ondje zazivaju Gospu i njezin blagoslov. P. Nagy dodaje da je riječ o istom načelu iz pisma: moliti se na javnim mjestima. Voditelj taj dio razgovora zaključuje riječju „predivno”.
sections.subtitle_en: Twice a day with a Rosary across Ban Jelačić Square
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fr. Božidar Nagy describes Merz's daily route across Ban Jelačić Square with a Rosary in his pocket
sections.content_en:
Merz did not only write about public prayer, but he also lived it. Fr. Nagy reveals a detail from his Zagreb daily life. Merz lived near the train station, in the **Starčevićev dom**, and worked at **Kaptol**, in the gymnasium. That is why **every day he crossed Ban Jelačić Square twice with a Rosary in his pocket** and prayed it on his way to work and from work.

The host recognizes in this a direct connection to today's practice of public prayer on the main Zagreb square. Merz, says the host, practically sanctified the Square with his Rosary prayer. That is precisely what the prayer warriors do today who invoke Our Lady and her blessing there. Fr. Nagy adds that this is about the same principle from the letter: praying in public places. The host concludes this part of the conversation with the word "wonderful".

sections.subtitle: Čudo iz 2018. čeka u Vatikanu: kako izgleda put do kanonizacije
sections.screenshot_description: P. Božidar Nagy objašnjava postupak priznavanja čuda pred trima komisijama
sections.content:
Na pitanje kada će Merz biti proglašen svetim, p. Nagy ne daje datum, ali izražava nadu. Hrvatska strana, kaže, ispunila je sve uvjete. Sva dokumentacija o **čudu koje se 2018. godine dogodilo na Merzovu grobu** predana je **Dikasteriju za kauze svetaca**, gdje sada čeka u redu da bude uzeta na proučavanje.

P. Nagy zatim objašnjava kojim putem svako čudo mora proći. Ono mora dobiti odobrenje **triju komisija**:

- **Liječnička komisija**: hrvatski liječnici već su sve odobrili (p. Nagy usput spominje da je bilo „zanimljivo kako je to išlo”), a sada slučaj moraju pregledati vatikanski liječnici.
- **Teološka komisija**: teolozi utvrđuju je li čudesno ozdravljenje doista povezano s blaženim Merzom, odnosno s njegovim zagovorom i posredovanjem.
- **Komisija biskupa i kardinala**: prema riječima p. Nagyja, ovaj je korak „više-manje formalan”.

Kada sve bude završeno, izdaje se **dekret o čudu**, čime se otvara „zeleno svjetlo” za kanonizaciju. Nakon toga je na mjesnoj Crkvi da se s papom dogovori kada će i gdje kanonizacija biti održana.
sections.subtitle_en: The 2018 miracle is waiting in the Vatican: what the path to canonization looks like
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fr. Božidar Nagy explains the procedure for recognizing a miracle before three commissions
sections.content_en:
To the question of when Merz will be canonized, Fr. Nagy does not give a date, but expresses hope. The Croatian side, he says, has fulfilled all the conditions. All documentation about the **miracle that occurred in 2018 at Merz's tomb** has been submitted to the **Dicastery for the Causes of Saints**, where it is now waiting in line to be taken up for study.

Fr. Nagy then explains which path every miracle must go through. It must receive the approval of **three commissions**:

- **Medical Commission**: Croatian doctors have already approved everything (Fr. Nagy mentions in passing that it was "interesting how that went"), and now Vatican doctors must examine the case.
- **Theological Commission**: theologians determine whether the miraculous healing is indeed connected to Blessed Merz, that is, to his intercession and mediation.
- **Commission of Bishops and Cardinals**: according to Fr. Nagy, this step is "more or less formal".

When everything is completed, a **decree on the miracle** is issued, which opens the "green light" for canonization. After that, it is up to the local Church to agree with the Pope on when and where the canonization will be held.

sections.subtitle: Slika predana papi i molitva svakog desetog u mjesecu
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj pripovijeda o predaji slike blaženog Ivana Merza papi u Rimu
sections.content:
Voditelj podsjeća na tisuće potpisa koje je mladež s Filipina uputila Svetom Ocu i u šali kaže da se novog papu „bombardira Merzom”. I njegova je zajednica tome pridonijela. Ove su godine imali, kako kaže, „priliku i čast i milost” biti u Rimu **25. ožujka, na svetkovinu Navještenja Blažene Djevice Marije**, i papi predati sliku blaženog Ivana Merza. Uz sliku su priložili molbu da se njihov zaštitnik što prije proglasi svetim. Kopiju slike namjeravaju izraditi i za sebe.

P. Nagy ističe da to iščekuju svi Merzovi štovatelji i da za tu nakanu treba moliti. U **Bazilici Srca Isusova** u Zagrebu svaki je **deseti dan u mjesecu** posvećen Merzu, jer je toga datuma završio svoj zemaljski život. Taj je dan, kaže, „na neki način njegov”, a tada se moli upravo za kanonizaciju. Svoju misao zaključuje s osmijehom: neka dragi Bog „malo požuri gore u Rimu”.
sections.subtitle_en: Painting presented to the Pope and prayer every tenth of the month
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host recounts the presentation of the painting of Blessed Ivan Merz to the Pope in Rome
sections.content_en:
The host recalls the thousands of signatures that the youth from the Philippines sent to the Holy Father and jokingly says that the new Pope is being “bombarded with Merz.” His community also contributed to this. This year they had, as he says, “the opportunity and the honor and the grace” to be in Rome **on March 25, on the solemnity of the Annunciation of the Blessed Virgin Mary**, and to present the Pope with a painting of Blessed Ivan Merz. Along with the painting, they attached a petition that their patron be declared a saint as soon as possible. They also intend to make a copy of the painting for themselves.

Fr. Nagy emphasizes that all of Merz's devotees await this and that one should pray for this intention. In the **Bazilika Srca Isusova** in Zagreb, every **tenth day of the month** is dedicated to Merz, because on that date he ended his earthly life. That day is, he says, “in a way his,” and on that day prayers are offered precisely for canonization. He concludes his thought with a smile: may dear God “hurry a bit up there in Rome.”

sections.subtitle: „Program života i rada”: od Orlova i Križara do izlaska iz katakombi
sections.screenshot_description: P. Božidar Nagy citira riječi pape Ivana Pavla II. s beatifikacije u Banjoj Luci
sections.content:
P. Nagy podsjeća na rečenicu koju smatra ključnom. Izgovorio ju je papa, danas svetac, **Ivan Pavao II.** u propovijedi na Merzovoj beatifikaciji u **Banjoj Luci**:

> „Ime Ivana Merza za cijeli jedan naraštaj mladih katolika značilo je program života i rada.”

To, ističe p. Nagy, mora vrijediti i danas. Raduje ga što se među mladima napokon bude inicijative koje Merza prihvaćaju.

Objašnjava i povijesni kontekst papinih riječi. Naraštaj o kojem je papa govorio bio je onaj iz Merzova vremena, kada je on bio na čelu **Orlovske katoličke organizacije**. Nakon nepravde koju je beogradski režim počinio **šestosiječanjskom diktaturom 1929.**, Orlovska je organizacija ukinuta. Njezini su se voditelji odmah reorganizirali i osnovali **Križarsku organizaciju**, po uzoru na tadašnje francuske euharistijske križare. Križari su preuzeli Merzovu baštinu i kao katolička udruga dodatno se razvili sve do 1945., a zatim je, kaže p. Nagy, „poznato što je slijedilo”.

Svoj pregled zaključuje slikom koja povezuje prošlost i sadašnjost: nakon 1945. hrvatski su katolici „išli u katakombe”, a sada iz njih izlaze.
sections.subtitle_en: “A Program of Life and Work”: from the Eagles and Crusaders to Emerging from the Catacombs
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fr. Božidar Nagy quotes the words of Pope John Paul II from the beatification in Banja Luka
sections.content_en:
Fr. Nagy recalls a sentence he considers crucial. It was spoken by the Pope, today a saint, **John Paul II**, in the homily at Merz's beatification in **Banja Luka**:

> “The name of Ivan Merz meant a program of life and work for an entire generation of young Catholics.”

This, Fr. Nagy points out, must hold true today as well. He is glad that initiatives that embrace Merz are finally awakening among the youth.

He also explains the historical context of the Pope's words. The generation the Pope spoke of was the one from Merz's time, when he was at the head of the **Orlovska katolička organizacija**. After the injustice committed by the Belgrade regime through the **January 6 Dictatorship of 1929**, the Orlovska organization was abolished. Its leaders immediately reorganized and founded the **Križarska organizacija**, modeled after the French Eucharistic crusaders of the time. The Crusaders took over Merz's heritage and, as a Catholic association, developed further until 1945, and then, says Fr. Nagy, “it is known what followed”.

He concludes his overview with an image that connects past and present: after 1945, Croatian Catholics “went into the catacombs”, and now they are coming out of them.

sections.subtitle: Blic pitanja: klanjanje ili propovijed, knjiga ili krunica
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj postavlja prvo blic pitanje, a p. Božidar Nagy razmišlja o odgovoru
sections.content:
Voditelj napominje da bi se o Merzu i njegovim suradnicima, koji su nakon njegove smrti prenosili njegovu ostavštinu, moglo još dugo govoriti. Izražava nadu da će ta tema doći na red u nekoj drugoj epizodi. Na kraju gostu postavlja nekoliko nenajavljenih **blic pitanja tipa „ili-ili”** i unaprijed upozorava da su neka „malo škakljiva” i provokativna.

**Tišina klanjanja ili propovijed pred punom crkvom?** P. Nagy odbija birati: „I jedno i drugo. Ne možete to odvojiti. To ide zajedno.” Voditelj se slaže da obje stvari imaju svoju vrijednost i moć.

**Knjiga u ruci ili krunica u ruci?** Ovdje gost ima jasan red prioriteta: „U prvom redu krunica u ruci”, a knjiga dolazi nakon nje. Voditelj dodaje da se za krunicu kaže kako je zapravo „malo evanđelje u ruci”, što p. Nagy potvrđuje.

**Duhovna disciplina ili spontanost u vjeri?** Odgovor p. Nagyja proizlazi iz isusovačke duhovnosti. Isusovci, kaže, imaju disciplinirani način molitve, jer treba znati red: kada, što i kako. Spontana molitva dolazi usput. Pritom navodi isusovačko načelo ***contemplativus in actione***, odnosno biti kontemplativan u djelovanju i povezati kontemplaciju, molitvu i svakodnevni rad.
sections.subtitle_en: Blitz questions: Eucharistic adoration or sermon, book or Rosary
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host asks the first blitz question, and Fr. Božidar Nagy ponders the answer
sections.content_en:
The host notes that one could speak for a long time about Merz and his collaborators, who carried on his legacy after his death. He expresses hope that this topic will have its turn in another episode. At the end, he asks the guest several unannounced **"either-or" blitz questions** and warns in advance that some are "a little tricky" and provocative.

**The silence of Eucharistic adoration or a sermon before a full church?** Fr. Nagy refuses to choose: "Both. You cannot separate that. It goes together." The host agrees that both things have their value and power.

**A book in hand or a Rosary in hand?** Here the guest has a clear order of priorities: "In the first place the Rosary in hand", and the book comes after it. The host adds that it is said of the Rosary that it is actually a "little gospel in hand", which Fr. Nagy confirms.

**Spiritual discipline or spontaneity in faith?** Fr. Nagy's answer stems from Jesuit spirituality. Jesuits, he says, have a disciplined way of prayer, because one needs to know the order: when, what, and how. Spontaneous prayer comes along the way. In doing so, he cites the Jesuit principle ***contemplativus in actione***, that is, being contemplative in action and connecting contemplation, prayer, and daily work.

sections.subtitle: Knjiga koja obraća i rad koji ne razdvaja katedru i pastoral
sections.screenshot_description: P. Božidar Nagy govori o knjigama Put k suncu i Zlatna knjiga kao izvorima obraćenja
sections.content:
**Dobra knjiga ili dobar duhovni razgovor?** P. Nagy ipak bira knjigu i objašnjava zašto. Kao primjer navodi **Put k suncu**, zbirku tekstova blaženog Merza. Zna za izričit slučaj: **Mišo Lukenda** iz zajednice **Nanovo rođeni** obratio se upravo na temelju te knjige i cjelokupnog Merza. Sve je to unio u svoju zajednicu, koja po uzoru na blaženika danas ima **formaciju na četiri razine**. Istu su knjigu prihvatili i **Mladi za domovinu u Sesvetama**.

Spominje i **Zlatnu knjigu**, koju je **kardinal Stepinac**, član Merzove Orlovske organizacije, nazvao „suhim zlatom”. Voditelj primjećuje da se ta knjiga ne zove bez razloga tako i zaključuje da dobra knjiga doista može biti dobar razgovor.

**Akademski ili pastoralni rad?** U posljednjem blic pitanju p. Nagy ponovno odgovara iz perspektive isusovačkog reda: to ide zajedno, jer i akademski rad jest, odnosno mora biti, pastoralni rad. Veličinu **svetog Ignacija Lojolskog** vidi upravo u tome što je od samih početaka osnivao brojne kolegije i gimnazije za odgoj i formaciju katoličke mladeži, kakve su postojale i u hrvatskim krajevima.

Zaključuje da je danas posebno važno da kršćani katolici ulaze u akademske krugove i povezuju ono što je povezivao Merz: **vjeru, znanost i kulturu**.
sections.subtitle_en: A book that converts and work that does not separate the chair and pastoral care
sections.screenshot_description_en: P. Božidar Nagy speaks about the books Put k suncu and Zlatna knjiga as sources of conversion
sections.content_en:
**A good book or a good spiritual conversation?** P. Nagy nevertheless chooses the book and explains why. As an example, he cites **Put k suncu**, a collection of texts by Blessed Merz. He knows of an explicit case: **Mišo Lukenda** from the community **Nanovo rođeni** converted precisely on the basis of that book and Merz as a whole. He brought all of this into his community, which, following the example of the blessed, today has **formation on four levels**. The same book was also adopted by **Mladi za domovinu in Sesvete**.

He also mentions **Zlatna knjiga**, which **Cardinal Stepinac**, a member of Merz's Eagle organization, called „pure gold”. The host notes that this book is not called that without reason and concludes that a good book truly can be a good conversation.

**Academic or pastoral work?** In the final quick question, p. Nagy again answers from the perspective of the Jesuit order: they go together, because academic work also is, that is, must be, pastoral work. He sees the greatness of **Saint Ignatius of Loyola** precisely in the fact that from the very beginning he founded numerous colleges and gymnasiums for the education and formation of Catholic youth, such as existed in Croatian regions as well.

He concludes that today it is especially important that Catholic Christians enter academic circles and connect what Merz connected: **faith, science, and culture**.

sections.subtitle: „Sve na veću slavu Božju”: zahvala i pogled prema sljedećoj epizodi
sections.screenshot_description: P. Božidar Nagy izgovara isusovačko geslo Omnia ad maiorem Dei gloriam
sections.content:
Voditelj zahvaljuje p. Nagyju na akademskom, pastoralnom i svakom drugom radu kojim se širi glas o blaženom Ivanu Merzu. Spominje i druge svece kojima se gost bavi, a za koje u razgovoru nije ostalo vremena. P. Nagy uzvraća zahvalom za poziv i završava geslom svoga reda: ***Omnia ad maiorem Dei gloriam***, „sve na veću slavu Božju”. Voditelj odgovara: „Amen.”

U odjavi voditelj gledatelje poziva da prate podcast ReDefinicija, da ga lajkaju, dijele i pretplate se, uz šaljivu opasku o „starohrvatskim” izrazima. Napominje i da je sljedeća epizoda već dostupna na profilu na Patreonu.

Na samom kraju slijedi isječak iz najave. Gost sljedeće epizode govori o tome kako se u staroj naciji, u kojoj su mnogi formirani u bivšem sustavu, negativan stav prema Hrvatskoj prenosi na djecu. Takav se stav, kaže, često ne uči izravno, nego ga djeca upijaju od roditelja, baka i djedova kao „vibru” jada i čemera. Zaključuje da, kao što Radu Borić „srce boli” kad vidi mlade kako idu na misu, njega srce boli kad vidi mlade koji su negativni i ponavljaju fraze koje bi teško izgovorili da ih tome netko, makar posredno, nije naučio.
sections.subtitle_en: "All for the greater glory of God": thanksgiving and a look toward the next episode
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fr. Božidar Nagy utters the Jesuit motto Omnia ad maiorem Dei gloriam
sections.content_en:
The host thanks Fr. Nagy for his academic, pastoral, and every other work by which word of Blessed Ivan Merz is spread. He also mentions other saints the guest deals with, for whom no time remained in the conversation. Fr. Nagy reciprocates with thanks for the invitation and concludes with the motto of his order: ***Omnia ad maiorem Dei gloriam***, "all for the greater glory of God". The host replies: "Amen."

In the sign-off, the host invites viewers to follow the podcast ReDefinicija, to like, share, and subscribe to it, with a humorous remark about "Old Croatian" expressions. He also notes that the next episode is already available on the Patreon profile.

At the very end, a clip from the preview follows. The guest of the next episode talks about how in an old nation, in which many were formed in the former system, a negative attitude toward Croatia is passed on to children. Such an attitude, he says, is often not taught directly, but children absorb it from parents, grandmothers, and grandfathers as a "vibe" of misery and bitterness. He concludes that, just as Rada Borić's "heart aches" when she sees young people going to Mass, his heart aches when he sees young people who are negative and repeat phrases they would hardly utter if someone, even if indirectly, had not taught them.
